statusDetail: Coverage-complete audit of six representative public paths and all 58 catalog checks.

page.framework: Server-rendered MPA with jQuery/Moment/Underscore and a web app manifest
page.notes: Persian RTL adult-content/community site. Audited public browsing, community, long-form, account-entry and failure-state archetypes. Authenticated posting/account management, photo detail pages and chat subdomain were not covered because they require credentials or are a separate origin; templates represented by sampled public routes were deduplicated.

paths.description: Homepage and global shell: purpose, navigation, preferences, metadata, security, performance and no-JS behavior.
Story listing archetype representing long, searchable collection pages.
Long-form content detail archetype selected from sitemap.xml.
Forum/index archetype representing community navigation and long tabular content.
Primary account form, labels, autofill, keyboard focus and invalid-submit behavior.

findings.summary: The site remains light when the user requests dark mode.
findings.evidence: The dark-condition screenshot is pixel-identical to the light screenshot; the probe reports color-scheme: normal and no color-scheme or prefers-color-scheme CSS.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme: light dark and provide preference-driven surface, text and control colors using prefers-color-scheme or light-dark().

findings.summary: High-contrast preferences do not receive an adapted treatment.
findings.evidence: Under prefers-contrast: more, links remain #80073f with no border or non-color cue; the CSS probe found no prefers-contrast or forced-colors rules.
findings.suggestedFix: Add high-contrast and forced-colors styles, preserve system colors, and ensure links and controls retain non-color affordances.

findings.summary: Cross-document navigation swaps abruptly with no transition treatment.
findings.evidence: The stylesheet probe found no view-transition-name or @view-transition rule across the MPA shell.
findings.suggestedFix: Progressively enhance same-origin navigation with @view-transition and restrained directional transitions, while respecting reduced motion.

findings.summary: Long listing and detail pages provide no responsive scroll-state orientation.
findings.evidence: The listing and detail DOMs are about 6,400 to 8,600 CSS px tall, while the CSS probe found no scroll-state, scroll timeline, or progress treatment.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a lightweight scroll progress/orientation affordance for long content, preferably declarative and disabled under reduced motion.

findings.summary: The mobile menu trigger is an unfocusable div rather than a button.
findings.evidence: At 360px the visible menu trigger is DIV role=navigation, tabindex=-1, has no name, and is only 25x29px. It cannot be operated with the keyboard.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace the trigger with a named button using aria-expanded and aria-controls; keep the nav landmark on the nav element.

findings.summary: Components rely only on page-level responsive rules.
findings.evidence: The complete CSS probe found no container-type or @container rules despite cards, tables, forms and navigation being reused in narrow and wide contexts.
findings.suggestedFix: Adopt container queries for reusable cards, tables and forms where their layout depends on available component width.

findings.summary: Key mobile controls are too small and one is pointer-only.
findings.evidence: The menu trigger measures 25x29px and tabindex=-1; desktop login/register links measure only 29x31px and 47x31px.
findings.suggestedFix: Use native controls, provide at least a 44x44 CSS-pixel hit area or sufficient spacing, and retain visible :focus-visible styles.

findings.summary: Unknown routes fall through to Chrome’s generic 404 page.
findings.evidence: A request to a nonexistent route returned HTTP 404 with an empty response, producing the browser error screen with no site navigation, explanation, search, or recovery link.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve a branded 404 document with a concise explanation, home/search actions, and the normal site navigation.

findings.summary: Nonessential legacy scripts are parser-blocking on every page.
findings.evidence: HAR/DOM confirmation shows jQuery 3.5.1, Moment, Underscore, global.js, lp.js and sharer.min.js are classic scripts without async/defer. The homepage still has a good 1.7s Lighthouse LCP, but this delivery pattern increases dependency cost.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove unused global libraries; defer remaining noncritical scripts and load route-specific behavior only where needed.

findings.summary: Third-party and legacy JavaScript dominate an otherwise small page.
findings.evidence: The HAR reports 350,952 transferred bytes, including 274,030 script bytes; 198,233 bytes are third-party and Google Tag Manager alone is 152,718 bytes.
findings.suggestedFix: Audit script usage, remove unnecessary jQuery/Moment/Underscore and tracking code, and conditionally load third parties after user value or consent.

findings.summary: The mobile navigation trigger has neither a valid control role nor an accessible name.
findings.evidence: The mobile probe identifies a nameless DIV with role=navigation and tabindex=-1 as the hamburger trigger.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a button with an accessible Persian label, aria-expanded and aria-controls; leave role=navigation on the containing nav.

findings.summary: Inline links are distinguishable only by low-contrast color.
findings.evidence: axe reports five serious link-in-text-block failures: #80073f links have only 1.21:1 contrast against surrounding #333 text and no underline or other cue.
findings.suggestedFix: Underline inline links and choose colors meeting text and non-text contrast requirements in all preference modes.

findings.summary: Pages lack a main landmark and heading hierarchy.
findings.evidence: axe and Lighthouse report no main landmark and no h1; the DOM probes show zero h1/h2 elements on homepage, listing, forum, login and detail samples.
findings.suggestedFix: Wrap primary content in main and add one descriptive h1 per template followed by a logical heading hierarchy.

findings.summary: Several important targets fall below a comfortable touch size.
findings.evidence: The menu trigger is 25x29px, login/register links are 29x31px and 47x31px, and the CAPTCHA refresh button is 37x37px. Reflow itself has no horizontal overflow.
findings.suggestedFix: Increase target boxes or spacing to at least 44 CSS pixels for primary mobile actions without preventing user zoom.

findings.summary: The logo has no intrinsic width and height attributes.
findings.evidence: The images primitive and Lighthouse unsized-images audit both identify /static/images/logo.png as missing width and height.
findings.suggestedFix: Add width and height attributes matching the source aspect ratio and retain responsive CSS sizing.

findings.summary: Chrome records unresolved inspector issues from the page’s cookie and third-party setup.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse best-practices scores 0.77 and inspector-issues fails; its third-party-cookies audit reports six cookies.
findings.suggestedFix: Resolve the reported cookie/security issues, update third-party integrations, and verify the DevTools Issues panel is clean.

findings.summary: Public pages omit canonical URLs.
findings.evidence: The metadata probe found no rel=canonical on the homepage; robots allows search and sitemap.xml lists a large public corpus, so canonical indexing signals are applicable.
findings.suggestedFix: Add an absolute self-referencing canonical URL per indexable page and keep it consistent with sitemap URLs.

findings.summary: Content pages have no structured or social-preview metadata.
findings.evidence: The homepage probe found zero JSON-LD blocks and no Open Graph tags; representative pages are public stories, forums and lists.
findings.suggestedFix: Add accurate Open Graph/Twitter metadata and schema.org JSON-LD for the organization and applicable story/article pages.

findings.summary: Session and analytics cookies are sent without Secure and with SameSite=None, and CSP/HSTS are absent.
findings.evidence: The headers primitive reports missing CSP and HSTS. All four observed cookies lack Secure; shsess is HttpOnly but SameSite=None.
findings.suggestedFix: Set Secure on all HTTPS cookies, use Lax/Strict unless cross-site use is essential, and deploy a restrictive CSP plus HSTS.

findings.summary: Tracking starts on load without an evident consent or minimisation boundary.
findings.evidence: The tracker probe finds four third-party origins including Google Analytics and an ad-tech origin; HAR attributes 198,233 of 350,952 transferred bytes to third parties.
findings.suggestedFix: Minimise analytics, remove opaque ad-tech calls, gate optional tracking on informed consent, and batch only essential events.

findings.summary: The account flow offers password-only authentication with no autofill tokens or passkey path.
findings.evidence: The login form exposes username/password fields but neither has autocomplete, and the page/source probes show no WebAuthn/passkey affordance.
findings.suggestedFix: Add username/current-password autocomplete immediately and offer passkey/WebAuthn registration and sign-in as a progressive enhancement.

findings.summary: Several browser-enforced defenses are missing or weak.
findings.evidence: Headers show no HSTS, CSP, or Permissions-Policy; Referrer-Policy is no-referrer-when-downgrade rather than a stricter origin policy. X-Frame-Options and nosniff are present.
findings.suggestedFix: Add HSTS, CSP with frame-ancestors, a least-privilege Permissions-Policy, and strict-origin-when-cross-origin or stricter referrer policy.

findings.summary: The site advertises an app manifest but deliberately unregisters every service worker.
findings.evidence: The manifest is valid, but the runtime probe reports no registrations and rendered source calls getRegistrations() then unregister() on every load, so there is no offline fallback.
findings.suggestedFix: Either remove the installability signal or add a scoped service worker with a minimal offline page and resilient cached shell.

findings.summary: HTTP failure recovery is not handled by the site.
findings.evidence: The unknown-route test returns a bare HTTP 404 and Chrome’s generic error document rather than a useful site state.
findings.suggestedFix: Return a small server-rendered 404 template with navigation, search, and retry/home recovery.

findings.summary: Sign-in fields omit autocomplete assistance.
findings.evidence: The username and password inputs have labels but no autocomplete attributes; the CAPTCHA answer is also unlabeled and placeholder-only.
findings.suggestedFix: Set autocomplete=username and autocomplete=current-password; give CAPTCHA input a persistent label and avoid obstructing password-manager workflows.

findings.summary: Background analytics and ad-tech work is disproportionate to the simple homepage.
findings.evidence: A 508-character homepage makes 21 requests; seven are third-party, including analytics, Cloudflare telemetry and four requests to coverdistilltile.com.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove nonessential telemetry/ad-tech and defer remaining analytics until consent or idle after the core experience.

findings.summary: Third parties consume most transferred bytes without visible user value.
findings.evidence: Third-party transfer is 198,233 bytes, 56% of the 350,952-byte homepage, while the visible page has one small logo and short text.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a third-party budget, remove opaque origins, and load analytics only when justified and cached/deferred.

taskList.title: Replace the mobile menu div with a named, keyboard-operable button and enlarge small targets

Remove or consent-gate opaque third parties and trim global legacy scripts
Add main landmarks, an h1 hierarchy, and robust inline-link cues
Add dark and high-contrast preference styles
Add a useful branded 404 recovery page
Improve sign-in autofill and add a progressive passkey option
Add canonical, Open Graph and appropriate structured metadata
Resolve lower-priority layout, asset, motion and installability gaps
